zechariah.11.p1.b1.text: Open your doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may consume your cedars! Wail, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen …

zechariah.11.p1.b2.text: Listen to the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is in ruins. Listen to the roaring of the young lions …

zechariah.11.p1.b3.text: Pasture the flock marked for slaughter, whose buyers slaughter them without remorse. … Even their own shepherds have no compassion on them.

zechariah.11.p1.b4.text: So I pastured the flock marked for slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. Then I took for myself two staffs, calling one Favor and the other Union, and I pastured the flock.

zechariah.11.p1.b5.text: And in one month I dismissed three shepherds. … I will no longer shepherd you. Let the dying die, and the perishing perish …

zechariah.11.p2.b1.text: Next I took my staff called Favor and cut it in two, revoking the covenant I had made with all the nations.

zechariah.11.p2.b2.text: If it seems right to you, give me my wages; but if not, keep them.

zechariah.11.p2.b3.text: So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.

zechariah.11.p2.b5.text: Then I cut in two my second staff called Union, breaking the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

zechariah.11.p2.b6.text: For behold, I will raise up a shepherd in the land who will neither care for the lost, nor seek the young, nor heal the broken … Woe to the worthless shepherd, who deserts the flock!
